topic.name: Volumes of Revolution Using the Washer Method: Rotation About Other Axes

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=-\dfrac 4 y$ and $x = y + 5$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about the line $x=-\dfrac{1}{2}.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.explanation:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

\begin{align*} -\dfrac{4}{y} & = y + 5\\[5pt] -4 & = y^2 + 5y \\[5pt] y^2 + 5y + 4 & = 0 \\[5pt] (y+1)(y+4) & = 0 \\[5pt] y & = -4, -1 \end{align*} Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=-4$ to $y=-1.$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=-\dfrac{4}{y},$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=y+5.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y+5.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left[\: \left(\color{blue}{y+5}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-\dfrac{1}{2}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left[ y+ \dfrac{11}{2} \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=-\dfrac{4}{y}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \big[\: \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left[\: \left(\color{brown}{-\dfrac{4}{y}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-\dfrac{1}{2}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} -\dfrac{4}{y} \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left[ y+\dfrac{11}{2} \right]^2 \, \textrm{d}y - \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} -\dfrac{4}{y} \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-4}^{-1} \left( \left[ y+\dfrac{11}{2} \right]^2 - \left[ \dfrac{1}{2} -\dfrac{4}{y} \right]^2 \right) \textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $y=\sqrt{x}$ and $y=x^3$ for $x \in [0,1]$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $y=2.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.explanation:
First, let's draw our vertical arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The vertical arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $y=\sqrt{x},$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $y=x^3.$

Now, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $y=x^3.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{\textrm{upper}}\right) - \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{lower}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{2}\right) - \left(\color{brown}{x^3}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[2 - x^3\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $y=\sqrt{x}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{\textrm{upper}}\right) - \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{lower}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \big[\: \left(\color{black}{2}\right) - \left(\color{blue}{\sqrt{x}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[2-\sqrt{x}\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{brown}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{blue}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[2 -x^3\right]^2 \, \textrm{d}x - \pi \int_{0}^{1} \left[ 2-\sqrt{x}\right]^2\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_0^1 \left((2-x^3)^2 - (2-\sqrt{x})^2\right)\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_0^1 \left(x^6 - 4 x^3 - x + 4 \sqrt{x} \right)\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] & = \pi\left. \left(\dfrac 1 7 \,x^7 - x^4 - \dfrac{1}{2}\,x^2 + \dfrac{8}{3}\, x^{3/2} \right)\right|_0^1\\[5pt] & = \pi \left[\left(\dfrac 1 7 \,(1)^7 - 1^4 - \dfrac{1}{2}\,(1)^2 + \dfrac{8}{3}\, (1)^{3/2} \right) - (0)\right]\\[5pt] & = \pi \left(\dfrac {55} {42}\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {55\pi}{42}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Horizontal Line

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=\dfrac{y^2}{2}+1$ and $x=y+1$ for $y \in [0,2]$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $x=-1.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.explanation:
First, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=\dfrac{y^2}{2}+1,$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=y+1.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=y+1.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{0}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{blue}{y+1}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-1}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{2} \left[y+2\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x={y}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{0}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{brown}{\dfrac{y^2}{2}+1}\right) - \left(\color{black}{{-1}}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{0}^{2} \left[ \dfrac{y^2}{2}+2 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_0^2 \left( \left[ y+2 \right]^2 - \left[\dfrac{y^2}{2}+2\right]^2 \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] & = \pi \int_0^2 \left( -\dfrac{y^4}{4} - y^2 + 4y \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] & = \pi\left. \left(-\dfrac{ y^{5}}{20} - \dfrac {y^3}{3} + 2 y^2 \right)\right|_0^2\\[5pt] & = \pi \left[\left(-\dfrac{ 2^{5}}{20} - \dfrac {2^3}{3} + 2 \cdot 2^2 \right) - 0 \right] \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {56\pi}{15} . \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Vertical Line

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $x=y^2$ and $(x+2)^2-7y^2 = 8$ for $x\geq0$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about the line $x=-2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.explanation:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical line, we need to solve the equation of our second curve for $x{:}$

\begin{align*} (x+2)^2-7y^2 &= 8 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = \sqrt{7y^2+8}-2 \end{align*}

Note that we take the positive root since $x \geq 0.$

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

\begin{align*} y^2 &= \sqrt{7y^2+8}-2 \\[5pt] y^2+2 &= \sqrt{7y^2+8} \\[5pt] (y^2+2)^2 &= 7y^2+8 \\[5pt] y^4+4y^2+4 &= 7y^2+8 \\[5pt] y^4-3y^2-4 &= 0 \\[5pt] (y^2-4)(y^2+1) &= 0 \\[5pt] (y-2)(y+2)(y^2+1) &= 0 \end{align*} Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=-2$ to $y=2.$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=y^2,$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=\sqrt{7y^2+8}-2.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=\sqrt{7y^2+8}-2.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{blue}{\sqrt{7y^2+8}-2}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-2}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left[ \sqrt{7y^2+8} \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=y^2.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{brown}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{brown}{y^2}\right) - \left(\color{black}{-2}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left[ y^2 + 2 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{brown}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left[ \sqrt{7y^2+8} \right]^2 \, \textrm{d}y - \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left[ y^2 + 2 \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-2}^{2} \left( 7y^2 + 8 - \left( y^2 + 2 \right)^2 \right) \textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

example.title: Identifying an Integral Representing the Volume of a Solid Generated by Rotation About a Vertical Line

question.text: The region enclosed by the curves $(x-4)^2+y^2=5$ and $3x+y=17$ for $y \in [-1,2]$ is rotated $2\pi$ radians about the line $x=4.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.explanation:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical line, we need to solve the equations of our curves for $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} (x-4)^2+y^2 &= 5 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = \sqrt{5-y^2}+4 \\[5pt] 3x+y &= 17 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x = \dfrac{17-y}{3} \end{align*}

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

The horizontal arrow

  • enters the region through the inner curve $x=\dfrac{17-y}{3},$ and

  • leaves through the outer curve $x=\sqrt{5-y^2}+4.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

  • Step I. Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=\sqrt{5-y^2}+4.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{blue}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{blue}{\sqrt{5-y^2}+4}\right) - \left(\color{black}{4}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[ \sqrt{5-y^2} \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step II. Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\dfrac{17-y}{3}.$

The corresponding volume is given by \begin{align*} {\color{red}V_{\text{inner}}} &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \big[\: \left(\color{red}{\textrm{right}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{\textrm{left}}\right) \:\big]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[\: \left(\color{red}{\dfrac{17-y}{3}}\right) - \left(\color{black}{4}\right) \:\right]^2\,\textrm{d}y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^{2} \left[ \dfrac{5-y}{3} \right]^2\,\textrm{d}y. \end{align*}

  • Step III. Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as \begin{align*} V &= {\color{blue}V_{\text{outer}}} - {\color{red}V_{\text{inner}}} \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^2 \left( \left( \sqrt{5-y^2} \right)^2 - \left( \dfrac{5-y}{3} \right)^2 \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] &= \pi \int_{-1}^2 \left( 5-y^2 - \dfrac{1}{9}(25-10y+y^2) \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \int_{-1}^2 \left( 45 - 9y^2 - 25 + 10y - y^2 \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \int_{-1}^2 \left( 20 + 10y - 10y^2 \right) \,\,\textrm d y \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left. \left( 20y + 5y^2 - \dfrac{10 y^3}3 \right)\right|_{-1}^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left( \left( 20\cdot2 + 5(2)^2 - \dfrac{10(2)^3}3 \right) - \left( 20\cdot(-1) + 5(-1)^2 - \dfrac{10(-1)^3}3 \right) \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left( \left( 40 + 20 - \dfrac{80}3 \right) - \left( -20 + 5 + \dfrac{10}3 \right) \right) \\[5pt] % &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left( 60 - \dfrac{80}3 + 15 - \dfrac{10}3 \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left( 75 - \dfrac{90}3 \right) \\[5pt] % &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left( 75 - 30 \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\pi}{9} \left( 45 \right) \\[5pt] &= 5\pi . \end{align*}
